thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - auth-anomaly detector triggered: surge of JWT reuse attempts from 185.92.45.0/24 hitting /v1/generate and /v1/session endpoints. rate=4k/min (baseline 20/min).

maya: paging oncall (I'm oncall SRE). seeing lots of 401s and some 200s with suspicious dup session ids.

leo: leo (sec-oncall) here, joining. any customer reports?

maya: not yet. auto-alert picked it up. initial aggregation: many requests include "x-session-id" patterns duplicated across different user_ids. sample log snippet:

```
2026-03-15T02:12:31Z service=auth req_id=abcd1234 ip=185.92.45.12 user_id=uid_123 x-session-id=AAAA-1111 status=200 path=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T02:12:32Z service=auth req_id=abcd1235 ip=185.92.45.45 user_id=uid_456 x-session-id=AAAA-1111 status=200 path=/v1/chat
```

maya: also found a debug log bundle uploaded at 2026-03-15T01:58 to s3://redwood-debug-temp/ with ACL not set properly. keys look like truncated session tokens.

jess: jess (platform) - I can lock that bucket immediately. running `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-debug-temp --acl private` now.

ops-bot: Deploy webhook: bucket-acl-locker v2 succeeded in 45s (deploy-id: dpl-9832).

maya: thanks. leo - can you confirm if these truncated tokens are usable to escalate?

leo: preliminary: truncated session fragments in logs are not full signing secrets, but we can't assume safety. two mitigations: 1) rotate auth signing key (k-id rotation) to invalidate JWTs created with old key; 2) roll forward a short TTL enforcement (force sessions >30m to re-auth). both have customer impact.

carol: carol (support) - will start drafting customer comms template. need impact scope (which orgs affected).

maya: running search across logs to map user_ids and IP hits. query: `grep -E "x-session-id=AAAA" -r /var/log/auth/*.log | awk '{print $6,$8,$11}' | sort | uniq -c`

maya: result (top 3):
```
52 hits: uid_123 ip=185.92.45.12 path=/v1/generate
47 hits: uid_456 ip=185.92.45.45 path=/v1/chat
3 hits: uid_998 ip=185.92.45.77 path=/v1/session
```

leo: looks like a small set of users. suggest immediate IP block for 185.92.45.0/24 at edge and rotate keys. I'll trigger the kill switch.

leo: running firewall rule add: `redwood-fwctl block ip 185.92.45.0/24 --reason "auth anomaly" --ticket 9876`

ops-bot: Firewall rule added: block-185-92-45 (propagated to all regions).

maya: I'm going to promote an emergency canary for auth-key rotation. plan: publish new key (k2), add to JWKS, set auth service to accept both k1 and k2 for 10m, then flip to require k2 only. that will force token refresh.

jess: prepping migration config. caution: some long-running batch jobs use service tokens with static keys; we'll coordinate with infra teams to update after rotation. tagging infra-admins.

leo: agree. also create a short-term audit of token issuance to identify which clients were issued JWTs in the window 01:45-02:15 UTC. run: `pg_dump query` placeholder and `SELECT token_id, user_id, issued_at FROM auth.tokens WHERE issued_at BETWEEN '2026-03-15 01:45' AND '2026-03-15 02:15';`

maya: executing now. preliminary count: 127 tokens issued in window, 9 of those map to the user_ids we saw duplicated.

carol: I'll reach out to those 9 accounts with a targeted note: "We’re investigating unusual session activity; we recommend signing out and re-authenticating." draft ready for review.

leo: legal on standby per policy. tagging @legal-team.

maya: quick mitigation checklist I ran:
- blocked IP range (ops-bot confirmed)
- locked S3 bucket ACL (jess confirmed)
- started auth key rotation (in progress)
- kicked long-lived sessions older than 24h (prepared but not yet executed)

jess: key rotation step 1 done: new key published to JWKS (jwks.k2) and propagated to edge caches. step 2 (require k2 only) scheduled in 8 minutes to allow graceful re-auth.

ops-bot: Auth service reload completed on canary nodes (50/50).

maya: monitoring metrics: token_validation_failures spiked as expected during canary but overall successful. no error budget burn.

leo: recommended next: invalidate service tokens issued with k1 for non-essential jobs. create rollout plan to update service principals.

carol: support outreach: sent targeted messages to the 9 impacted accounts, and a broader notice to customers who had sessions in that time window (~120 accounts) with a templated advisory.

maya: incident status: MITIGATED -> external-facing impact minimal; suspected exfil of full tokens = LOW (no evidence). internal severity: P2 -> we'll keep pager until rotation completes and audit finished.

leo: follow-ups: postmortem runbook, ensure debug log uploader requires MFA and blocks public ACLs by policy, add an automated check to deny public ACLs on debug buckets.

maya: agreed. creating incident ticket: INC-2026-345 (assigning to maya, leo, jess, carol).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 created and assigned. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-345

carol: thanks team. I'll keep support channel updated with timeline and customer responses.

maya: handing off to leo for sec follow-up and to jess for infra cleanup. I'm off-call in 20m but will check updates.

leo: I'll own the post-rotate audit and confirm no token misuse. will post summary here once complete.

ops-bot: scheduled job: revoke-old-sessions (run in 12 minutes).

maya: mid-priority note - make sure we rotate service keys for batch jobs this week.

leo: update 02:28 UTC - post-rotate audit complete: no sign of token replay beyond the duplicates we blocked; no customer data exfil observed. I'll file a detailed sec report.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 status: RESOLVED (2026-03-15T02:34:59Z). Severity downgraded to MONITOR.

jess: created follow-up tasks: RBAC for debug uploads, ACL hardening, alert tuning for session duplication.

carol: sending final customer note now.

maya: good job. closing thread after postmortem doc published. :thumbsup:
